Spawn Jumpman through$436A, repeatedly collect bombs through$436D, wait for the death controller to finish, respawn while reserve lives remain, otherwise call cleanup and use the elimination vector$3032. Zero remaining bombs freezes movement and uses completion vector$3030.

On a player tick, collision is lethal only when no sprite bits3-7 are present and one of hazard bits1-2 is present, with life state0. Then tail-jump$348B to drain one queued bitmap change. Sprite bombs4-7 are handled separately as collectibles.

Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

18 seven-byte records [coarse key,x,y,callback low/high,post-draw low/high]. Terminator: $FF. Coordinates are160-wide bitmap positions. The resident scanner matches the key, calls both hooks, adds $3015 points, erases the bomb, follows the draw pointer and decrements $3013. This list is not bounded by the target counter.

Require hazard pulse, and reject life state2; dying state1 is accepted. Scan sprites7..4 for a collision snapshot containing player bit0. Disable the first matching flying bomb, queue collection sound, add100 to24-bit score, update HUD/extra life, decrement remaining bombs and return. With no match, branch through$3385 to landing scan$32E5. Controlled CPU/native checks cover life0/1/2 and pulse0; a neutral-input native replay also collects during life1. With supplied remaining count0 and a flying-bomb collision, unchanged CPU and native code decrement the count to255. This is a controlled input, not a demonstrated gameplay underflow. The collector itself therefore cannot justify an unconditional twelve-collection cap.

Inputs A=new occupancy, FB/FC=drawing pointer,Y=location index. Append six bytes [occupancy,pointer high,pointer low,x,y,index] at$34DA+8-bit offset, then add6 modulo256. No capacity guard. Controlled placements preserve43 pending records; record44 starts at offset2 and overlaps earlier records.  A conservative scheduler model bounds pending records at eight for normal speed selections 2 through 8: four actors, at least 13 flight updates before landing, one collection per pulse, and at least two pop-service calls between pulses. Speed 1 is outside that bound; no natural overload is established. A bounded speed1 stress executes original initialization for128 seeds and four supplied collection policies:512 scenarios, at most1000 pulses each, collector/landing then spawn/move then one pop. Maximum pending count is4. Native execution matches the sampled peak. Player movement, static pickups and interrupt interleavings are omitted, so this does not bound every legal speed1 run.
Eight-bit next-record offset, not an unbounded byte count. Enqueue adds6 modulo256; service subtracts6 modulo256. Zero is treated as empty, including after128 uninterrupted enqueues.

Pop one six-byte entry last-in-first-out, update its occupancy, patch placement or erasure stream coordinates, play corresponding sound, save renderer context, draw, restore context. The collision callback tail invokes this service even without a hazard pulse. Zero offset returns without popping. Controlled native comparisons cover depth43, overlapping depth44 and apparent-empty depth128; no ordinary overload route is established. The speed divider has steady period equal to the selected speed, including one service per pulse at speed 1. The bounded model covers speeds 2 through 8 only.

Runtime six-byte edit stack addressed from$34DA by an8-bit offset. With even offsets reachable by repeated +/-6, indexed field stores can reach$35DD. Initial bytes match retained PLF06 tail, not initialized bomb records. No capacity guard: the44th uninterrupted enqueue overlaps early records;128 enqueues wrap the offset to apparent empty. Those are forced backlog checks.

Retained file bytes, identical at these addresses to PLF06. Donor boundary comes from PLF06 $3491-$37FF (unused_shooting_pattern_tail): Unused loaded 00/FF memory-fill pattern after the projectile loop; identical byte-for-byte to PLF03 at the same addresses. No reachable script/table points into this tail. This copy has no established active control-flow or drawing target; it remains byte data.
